prompt: Image 1 is a layout guide. Keep its geography exactly, in the same positions and sizes: the band of mountains across the upper half, the large lake on the left with the river running from it down to the bottom edge, the big forest on the right, the smaller woods on the left and bottom, the rolling hills, the dash-dot frontier line across the lower part, the little scattered houses near the bottom centre, the small town with towers at the bottom centre and the colossal wall running along the whole bottom edge. The six small red circles in image 1 only mark positions; never paint the circles. At each of them, from the bottom of the image to the top, paint a small landmark, small enough to leave room for a marker on top: (1, lowest) a tiny abandoned hamlet of five dark houses with no lights, its edges fading into bare paper as if being erased; (2, right, at the forest edge) a forest road broken by enormous twisted roots; (3, centre-left) a small village ringed by a wooden palisade, with tiny tents around it; (4, right, between mountains) a narrow rocky gorge with a path through it; (5, upper left) the half-buried ruin of an ancient temple of huge cyclopean stone blocks and broken columns, with a dark stairway going down (not an igloo, not a dome of ice); (6, top) a patch where the map itself is erased: bare white paper with ink lines dissolving into it and a faint violet stain. Repaint it as a hand-painted fantasy map in the exact technique and palette of image 2: loose black dip-pen ink linework over transparent watercolor washes, granulating indigo and night-blue pigment, moonlit pale highlights, warm ochre accents, cold-press paper texture visible. It is night: the whole map is bathed in deep indigo and blue-grey washes, mountains drawn as little ink peaks with slate shading, forests as clusters of small ink trees in dark teal, the lake and river catching silver moonlight, the town at the bottom with a few warm lit windows, the wall in pale grey stone blocks. The top of the map fades into a dark violet-indigo bloom. Seen from above like an old explorer's map, a premium illustrated board-game map. Draw the mountains as varied, organic, hand-drawn peaks of different sizes and shapes with ink hatching and painted shadows, never identical repeated triangles; forests as rich painted masses of tree crowns with depth; hills as soft brushed swells. Lots of painterly variation and hand-made imperfection, like a master illustrator's map. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no compass rose, no cartouche, no frame, no border, no scale bar, no people. Full bleed: the painting covers the whole image edge to edge.
